Module designation: Not really mentioned. For water meters under R49, module designation isn't typical. Omit or set null. The schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll omit since not present... Actually rule 8 says don't fabricate; omit if not present. I'll omit.

Description: "A volumetric water meter" — could put in description.

Recommendation:
- R 49-1: 2006 → canonical id "R49", edition 2006... wait, R49-1:2006. The id should be canonical "R49", edition 2006, amendment null. Accuracy classes: ["2"] — accuracy class 2. Actually for water meters, accuracy class is 2 (metering). Also flow profile sensitivity class U0/D0. Accuracy classes: ["2"].

Hmm, edition: R49-1: 2006 → edition 2006, part 1. The schema just has edition (int). I'll set edition: 2006. Maybe include part info? Not in schema. I could note in id... The instruction says canonical e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". So id: "R49". Maybe "R49-1"? The example shows R49-1 is a part of R49. I think "R49" with edition 2006 is fine. Hmm, but the certificate specifically references R 49-1: 2006. I'll use id "R49" and edition 2006. Actually, to be more precise, maybe include part. The schema doesn't have part. I'll keep id as "R49".

Footnotes:

Characteristics:

Type level (Table 1 & 2 general):
- measuring_principle: "Volumetric"
- accuracy_class: 2 (dimensionless)
- temperature_range_ambient: {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C
- water_temperature_class: "T30" with range (+0,1 °C / +30 °C). This is T30 class meaning water temperature from 0.1°C to 30°C. I could record as value string "T30" or structured: water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 30} °C. Hmm. The value "T30 (+0,1 °C / +30 °C)". I'll record water_temperature_class: "T30" (string) and maybe water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 30} °C. Both fine. I'll do both.
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa (16 bar). Record as value 1.6, unit "MPa". Could also note 16 bar. I'll just do MPa: value 1.6, unit MPa.
- orientation: "All positions (Horizontal, vertical or diagonal)" — string value.
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)" — string. Could split into upstream and downstream. I'll keep as string: "U0/D0". Hmm, keep "U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)". Maybe simpler: value "U0/D0". I'll use "U0 and D0" with maybe separate description. Let me just keep full string but cleaned: "U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)".
- reverse_flow: "The sensor is not intended to measure reverse flow" — string value.
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 63 (0,63 bar)" → value "Δp 63" or structured: pressure_loss max 0.63 bar. I'll record pressure_loss_class: "Δp63" string, and maybe pressure_loss: {max: 0.63} bar. I'll do pressure_loss_class: "Δp 63 (0.63 bar)". Hmm, rule about numbers... it's a class designation, string is acceptable. I'll do two entries: pressure_loss_class: "Δp63", and pressure_loss: {min null, max 0.63} bar.

Additional characteristics (Table 2) for Hybrid III/IV/V registers:
- environmental_class: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" — string. Actually M1 is environmental class, O is... "M1/O" locates. Keep string "M1 / O (installed outdoors)".
- electromagnetic_environment: "E1"
- power_supply: "Non-replaceable battery (2.5 – 3.75 V)". Split: power_supply_type: "Non-replaceable battery", power_supply_voltage: {min: 2.5, max: 3.75} V.

Software identification — this is config-level / component-level: registers Hybrid III, IV, V with versions and checksums. This could be recorded as components (registers) or matrix. The schema: components[] with role, type_designations, characteristics. Hmm. These registers are indicating device variants. Let me think.

Table 4 gives indicating device characteristics per meter name × register variant. That's a matrix table. Table 3 gives flow characteristics per meter name (V100/V200) × ratio Q3/Q1 (80 or 200). So the models: V100, V110, V200, V210, with register variants.

Model family: The cert covers a family: models V100, V110, V200, V210. Each with register variants.

Table 3 rows: V100 (3.25 RPL, Q1 0.125, Q2 0.200, Q3 10, Q4 12.5, ratio 80), V200 (same), V100 (Q1 0.080, Q2 0.128, Q3 16, Q4 20, ratio 200), V200 (same). So flow characteristics vary by meter (V100/V200 — but values identical between V100 and V200; the difference is ratio Q3/Q1: 80 vs 200).

So config-level: flow rates depend on ratio choice. I could model as config_level entries with axis "Q3/Q1 ratio" with conditions "Q3/Q1 = 80" and "Q3/Q1 = 200".

Table 4: indicating range and verification scale interval per meter × register variant.

Let me structure:

model_family:
- family_name: null (no explicit family name; text says "family of instruments")
- models: V100, V110, V200, V210. Each model_id. Labels maybe "V100" etc. Attributes: maybe note register variants in attributes? I'll keep simple.

Actually, wait: Table 3 lists only V100 and V200. Table 4 lists V100, V110, V200, V210. The certified type identification says "Type: V100 and V200". V110/V210 may be sub-variants (perhaps with different pulse output?). To be safe, models: V100, V110, V200, V210.

model_level characteristics from Table 3 (for V100/V200):
- revs_per_liter: 3.25 (rev/liter) — same for all; it's type level? It's in the family table with same value. The nominal capacity 3.25 rev/liter. Could be type_level: revolutions_per_liter: 3.25 unit "rev/liter".

- q2_transitional_flow: 0.200 or 0.128 m³/h
- q3_permanent_flow: 10 or 16 m³/h
- q4_overload_flow: 12.5 or 20 m³/h
- ratio_q3_q1: 80 or 200

Since the variation axis is Q3/Q1 ratio (a configuration choice — note text says flow rates can be freely chosen within constraints), config_level is most appropriate:
- attribute "minimum_flow_rate_q1", axis "q3_over_q1_ratio", values: [{condition: "Q3/Q1 = 80", value: 0.125, unit m³/h}, {condition: "Q3/Q1 = 200", value: 0.080}]
- similarly q2, q3, q4.
- attribute "ratio_q3_over_q1" axis same: values [{condition "Q3/Q1 = 80", value 80}, {condition..., value 200}]. Hmm, that's circular but fine. Actually ratio_q3_q1 IS the axis. I can include it as config condition only. I'll include attribute entries anyway for completeness? Maybe cleaner: put the axis as "q3_q1_ratio" and include q3_q1_ratio as attribute too. Eh, it's the axis itself; I'll include it with values 80 and 200 for both models V100 and V200. Since values identical across V100/V200, config-level is the right choice.

Also, both V100 and V200 share identical flow values, so model_level for these would duplicate. Config-level is better.

Table 4 is meter × register variant matrix → matrix_tables entry:
name: "General characteristics of the indicating device"
columns: ["meter_name", "register_variant", "indicating_range_minimum", "verification_scale_interval"]
column_units: [null, null, "m³", "m³"]
rows: 8 rows.

Also model_level entries for indicating_range and verification_scale_interval per model? The variation is per register variant (config), so config_level:
- attribute "indicating_range_minimum", axis "register_variant", values: [{condition "V100 4x4 Register", value 9999.99999, unit m³}, ...] — that's 8 conditions. Or I can leave it in matrix_tables only. The schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. Table 4 fits matrix_tables well. I could additionally add config_level for verification_scale_interval. To keep it clean, I'll put Table 4 in matrix_tables and also add config_level entries keyed by register_variant since attributes vary by configuration (register variant), with condition including meter name.

Hmm, conditions like "V100 / 4x4 Register" etc. That's reasonable.

Actually let me reconsider: maybe better to treat the register variants as components (indicating device variants) — e.g., components: role "indicating device (register)", type_designations ["4x4 Register", "5x3 Register", "Mechanical", "Hybrid III Register", "Hybrid IV Register", "Hybrid V Register"]. And the software table (Table 2) gives software IDs for Hybrid III/IV/V registers — components characteristics.
